# Test 20261012-233033-d983: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | Turn 2; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44 | The tester asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`, creating `RS-06F972` with `"left": 2` and `RS-712EFD` with `"left": 1`. This holds two items and breaks the rule, "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The retry loop runs twice without stopping on success. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; app.py:72; RULES.md:6 | The reply says, "I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 under reservation ID RS-712EFD." The stock service actually created two reservations of one item each for that order. The tool returns only the second reservation and the requested `qty`, concealing the extra hold. The reported total disagrees with the recorded backend state and the rule that the agent tells the customer how many items it reserved. |

## Notes

Checked all three turns and their model/tool/backend records using `nookku transcript --trace --test 20261012-233033-d983`. The transcript reports, "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Read findings.json and audit.json: no automated findings, audit breaks, errors, or blocked calls were recorded. These results do not detect the duplicate successful reservation.

Read RULES.md and all six Python project files. Checked current stock.json and state.json with read-only commands. stock.json corroborates two reservations for order 6210, `RS-06F972` and `RS-712EFD`, each with `"qty": 1`, and one teapot set left. Current project state is supporting evidence; the sealed backend records independently establish both issues. The stock replies in turns 1 and 3 match their GET results.

No app-state snapshot files were available in the test folder. No project test files were present in the file listing. Did not start the app, send it messages, or mutate its state. Only this report was written. Return, refund, and order-privacy behavior were not exercised by this test.
answer:
Found two issues: the app reserved two sets instead of one, then reported only one reservation.
The test seal is intact; the audit found no altered exchanges.
